title: Software and technical knowledge
description: Repositories, applications, components, libraries, APIs, environments, releases, bugs and design decisions (ADRs), with how they depend on each other. For engineering notes and technical documentation.

entity_types.name: Repository
entity_types.description: A source code repository. Use for: git repos by name or URL. Not for: the application it builds (Application). Examples: 'org/website', 'infra-config'.

entity_types.name: Application
entity_types.description: A deployable software product or service that the team builds or runs. Not for: third-party libraries (Library) or the repo (Repository). Examples: 'billing-api', 'mobile app'.

entity_types.name: Component
entity_types.description: A module, package or subsystem inside an application. Not for: a whole application. Examples: 'auth module', 'payment worker'.

entity_types.name: Library
entity_types.description: A third-party or shared library, framework or SDK used as a dependency. Not for: the team's own deployable software (Application) or a language (Language). Examples: 'React 19', 'SQLAlchemy', 'pydantic'.

entity_types.name: Language
entity_types.description: A programming language or runtime. Not for: libraries or frameworks written in it (Library). Examples: 'Python 3.12', 'TypeScript', 'Node 26'.

entity_types.name: Api
entity_types.description: An interface that other software calls: HTTP endpoints, RPC, MCP tools, events. Not for: the application that offers it (Application). Examples: 'POST /api/recall', 'GraphQL schema'.

entity_types.name: Environment
entity_types.description: A deployment target: production, staging, a cluster or a region. Not for: a single server or an application. Examples: 'production', 'staging EU'.

entity_types.name: Release
entity_types.description: A versioned release of an application or library, with its date. Not for: a general change that has no version (Decision). Examples: 'v0.5.0 (2026-10-25)'.

entity_types.name: Bug
entity_types.description: A defect or incident in software, with its symptom and cause. Use for: reported or found problems. Not for: planned work (Task). Examples: 'login loop on Safari', 'memory leak in worker'.

entity_types.name: Decision
entity_types.description: A technical or architectural decision with its rationale (ADR). Not for: open questions or plans not yet decided. Examples: 'Use Postgres for the job queue', 'Drop Python 3.9'.

entity_types.name: Concept
entity_types.description: A technical idea, pattern or standard that is explained in the notes. Not for: concrete software (Application, Library). Examples: 'event sourcing', 'OIDC PKCE flow'.

entity_types.name: Document
entity_types.description: A spec, README, design doc, RFC or runbook that can be cited. Not for: the thing it describes. Examples: 'ARCHITECTURE.md', 'RFC 6749'.

entity_types.name: Person
entity_types.description: A developer, maintainer or reporter. Not for: teams or companies (Organization). Examples: 'maintainer Ana'.

entity_types.name: Organization
entity_types.description: A company or open-source project behind a tool or service. Not for: a single person. Examples: 'GitHub', 'Mozilla'.

edge_types.name: DependsOn
edge_types.description: A repository, application, component or library requires another to build or run.

edge_types.name: Uses
edge_types.description: An application or component makes use of a library, language, API or service.

edge_types.name: WrittenIn
edge_types.description: A repository, application or component is implemented in a language.

edge_types.name: PartOf
edge_types.description: A component belongs to an application; an application is built from a repository.

edge_types.name: Implements
edge_types.description: A component or application implements an API, concept or decision.

edge_types.name: Exposes
edge_types.description: An application or component offers an API.

edge_types.name: DeployedTo
edge_types.description: An application or release runs in an environment.

edge_types.name: ReleasedIn
edge_types.description: A change, fix or feature shipped in a release.

edge_types.name: CausedBy
edge_types.description: A bug was caused by a component, library, release or decision.

edge_types.name: FixedBy
edge_types.description: A bug was fixed by a release or decision.

edge_types.name: Affects
edge_types.description: A bug impacts an application, component or environment.

edge_types.name: Supersedes
edge_types.description: A decision, release or document replaces an earlier one.

edge_types.name: DocumentedIn
edge_types.description: An entity is described in a document.

edge_types.name: MaintainedBy
edge_types.description: A person or organization maintains a repository, application or library.

edge_types.name: RelatesTo
edge_types.description: LAST RESORT. Use only when two entities are clearly associated and no other relation type in the list fits. Never use it when a more specific type applies.

instructions: Software and technical notes. Use the MOST SPECIFIC type: a git repo is a Repository, something deployed is an Application, a third-party dependency is a Library, a defect is a Bug, an architectural choice with a reason is a Decision. Extract DependsOn/Uses for dependencies, WrittenIn for languages, DeployedTo for environments, ReleasedIn/FixedBy for versions and fixes, and Supersedes when something replaces an earlier decision or release. Record versions and dates when stated. Never extract secrets, tokens or keys. Use only the listed relation types and prefer a specific one over RelatesTo.
